page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.8-128 is a flexible virtual machine instance configured for memory-intensive computing tasks. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7742 processor running at 2.25 GHz, it supplies 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. The hardware configuration couples this compute capacity with 128 GB of system memory, yielding an elevated allocation ratio of 8 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Storage and acceleration tradeoffs define the system architecture. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes to handle operating system and persistent data needs. It also lacks hardware GPU accelerators. For network connectivity, the instance provides one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio delivers high memory capacity without the cost overhead of provisioning unneeded compute cores. This profile is engineered for memory-bound workloads, such as enterprise relational databases, distributed caching nodes, memory-heavy batch pipelines, and data analytics engines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.8-128 is a flexible memory-optimized compute instance driven by the AMD EPYC 7742 processor. Operating at 2.25 GHz across 8 physical x86_64 cores with multithreading enabled, it delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128 GB of RAM. This configuration provides a high memory allocation ratio of 8 GB per virtual core. The server includes no integrated local drive storage or hardware GPU accelerators, directing persistent storage operations to network-attached block volumes. A complimentary public IPv4 address is included. Designed to balance memory capacity against core density, VM.Standard.E3.Flex.8-128 serves environments such as in-memory caches, enterprise relational databases, ETL routines, and memory-constrained application serving.
